text:
Chicago arrives in Detroit having just snapped a three-game winless run with a 2-1 win over LAK, though they sit 2-3-0 over their last five and have been outscored 15-9 in that stretch. Detroit won 4-3 at EDM in a shootout after trailing in the third, but plays without Albert Johansson, Mason Appleton and Marco Kasper. The human story belongs to Patrick Kane, back in Detroit for the first time since leaving the Red Wings after 189 games, and one assist from 900 for his career.

The numbers favor the home side. At five on five, DET has taken 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) and CHI 41%, and our model has DET ahead 3.21 to 2.77 tonight. Both teams are better than their records: finishing has cost each, and CHI's goaltending has too. On special teams, DET's power play generates 0.87 expected goals a game to CHI's 0.55, though DET takes 4.4 penalties a game. In net, projected starter Spencer Knight is 1.3 goals saved above expected this season (11.1 last year), while John Gibson is at -4.3 this year after +10.1 last year.

Connor Bedard is our top CHI scoring pick at 34%, and Alex DeBrincat leads DET at 38%. Kane is at 22% to score after eleven games without one on 2.6 expected goals. As a pair of under-the-radar picks, we like Roman Kantserov, 53% for a point on a line that creates chances, and Michael Brandsegg-Nygård, who has had dangerous shots lately and is 19% to score.
